newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada base metals rise on hopes for metal prices.
newsitem.headline: Canada base metals rise on hopes for metal prices.

text.p: Base metal stocks bounded ahead on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday amid investor confidence that base metal prices are on their way up, analysts said.
The TSE base metal index was up 1.45 percent in the first two hours of trading.

Nickel concerns Inco Ltd and Falconbridge Ltd were both higher, with Inco up C$0.85 to C$48.75 and Falconbridge gaining C$0.40 to C$32. Alcan Aluminium Ltd rose C$0.85 to C$48.80 and Rio Algom Ltd gained C$1.05 to C$34.15.
"Metal prices are on the right trend, and that gets the trend going for the metal stock prices," said analyst Terry Ortslan of Ortslan and Associates in Montreal.

The sector has risen steadily in recent weeks on hopes that copper, zinc and nickel prices will improve this year, analysts said. While the base metal subindex took a dive with the rest of the stock market on Wednesday following remarks from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, it rapidly made up for the dip on Thursday.

"If Mr. Greenspan is worried in the U.S. about asset prices, he is worried about a strong economy," said analyst David Charles with Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion. "The key there is a strong economy. If you believe the growth is there, that should be good for metal demand and metal prices."
Rio Algom and Inmet Mining Corp were both higher on Thursday after announcing a large increase in resources at their shared Antamina copper and zinc project in Peru. Inmet was up C$0.40 tto C$8.70.
Interim drill results have set the resource at Antamina at a minimum of 400 million tonnes of ore up from previous estimates of 129 million tonnes.
"There are a lot of challenges with this particular property...but they're all surmountable," said Ortslan.
"The good news is the tonnage is up and they seem to be on the ball."
